source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #289 (branch fix/126-resource-limits at head 309336fe34702b554195d9dfdc08adf7863ddddb — branch commits 36fb96d (embedder-configurable resource limits via LimitsConfig (#126)), 457b209 (enforce the total-page ceiling on host-side memory growth), e38f6ee (preflight the aggregate memory minimum before allocating) and 309336f (preflight table limits before allocating; claim initial pages atomically), plus merge commit f77c527 bringing in current main 20e7e94 and re-baseline commits 8feafcd and 6eb3b67, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45285608348 and 45285626265 against the branch and pull-request run 45285593690, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for the third and fourth review findings on PR #289 (#126). Third: with both the total-page and table-element ceilings configured, instantiation created (and adopted) the module's memories before it ever checked the defined tables, so a module refused for an oversized table left its memories — and their charged pages — in the store permanently; every limit check instantiation performs (table minima and the memory aggregate) now completes before any memory or table is created. Fourth: the aggregate preflight compared a read of the store total against the ceiling and the memories then registered their initial pages with an unconditional addition, but a shared memory can grow through a retained handle without taking the store's runtime lock, so a racing growth could claim the last page between the check and the registration and push the total past the ceiling; the preflight is now a single atomic claim on the shared page budget (a reservation the creation loop pays each memory out of, releasing any unspent remainder on failure), and adoption itself charges initial pages through the same claim, refusing without residue when the budget is full. Regression tests cover a table-refused module followed by a module using the whole memory cap, budget claims under contention stopping exactly at the cap, and concurrent shared growth racing adoptions. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (20e7e94) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45285648242, gate success): it reproduces the pre-#126 baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, and the only code change since the previous baseline on this branch is the 309336f commit, so every delta below is that commit's own. The deltas are the reservation/claim plumbing and the moved table check: in release, stripped file grows +48 B in core-aot and core-jit to +368 B in component (stripped .text −32 B in core-aot and core-jit to +256 B), and in release-size stripped file grows +128 B in core-nosimd to +528 B in core-jit (stripped .text +64 B to +432 B); the baseline configuration, which links no telomere code, is byte-identical in both profiles. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series, now at +9.59% (2,433,656 B to 2,667,136 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
